title: Heat and Temperature
seo_title: Primary 4 Science: Heat and Temperature Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_text: Recognise that heat is a form of energy and that temperature is a measure of the degree of hotness of an object, measured with a thermometer in °C. Show that heat flows from a hotter to a colder place or object, and recognise the effects of heat gain and heat loss: temperature change, expansion and contraction, and change of state (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on heat and temperature: reading thermometers, heat flow, expansion and contraction, and cooling experiments. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Heat flows from hotter to colder things.
key_sub: Temperature tells us how hot or cold something is.
body_html:
How to think about it

Heat is a form of energy. Temperature tells us how hot or cold something is.

  • Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius (°C) with a thermometer.
  • Heat flows from a hotter object to a colder one until both are at the same temperature. Cold does not flow.
  • Gaining heat: temperature rises, things expand, solids may melt. Losing heat: temperature falls, things contract, liquids may freeze.
Example

A cup of 90 °C tea is left in a 28 °C room. What happens?

Heat flows from the tea to the air

The tea cools until it reaches 28 °C

Answer: It cools to about 28 °C.

Example

A dented ping-pong ball is put in hot water. Why does the dent pop out?

The air inside gains heat

The air expands

Answer: The air expands and pushes out the dent.

Common mistakes

  • Saying 'cold flows into' something. Heat flows out of the warmer object.
  • Thinking heat and temperature are the same. A bathtub of warm water has more heat than a cup at the same temperature.
  • Thinking things expand when they lose heat. They contract.
  • Reading a thermometer from above or below the liquid level.

faq.q: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
faq.a: Heat is a form of energy. Temperature is a measure of how hot or cold something is. A large pot of water and a small cup can have the same temperature, but the pot has more heat.
No. Heat flows from the hotter object to the colder one. When you hold ice, your hand loses heat to the ice.

faq.q: Why do things expand when heated?
faq.a: Most solids, liquids and gases get bigger when they gain heat and smaller when they lose heat. That is why railway tracks have gaps.
